MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  March 2, 2015

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the
Library Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor
Schlicht at 5:01 p.m., on March 2, 2015, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on February 25, 2015, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also
posted at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and the Norman
P. Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Bucknum
  Council Member Sachs
  Council Member Ury
  Mayor Pro Tem Raths
  Mayor Schlicht

Absent:  None

Staff Present:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services
  Cheryl Dyas, Director of Administrative Services
  Karen Hamman, City Clerk

RECESS

At the hour of 5:02 p.m., Mayor Schlicht declared a recess. The City Council reconvened at 6:00
p.m. with all five City council Members present.

INVOCATION: Mayor Pro Tem Raths

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Council Member Ury

City Council Minutes  1  March 2, 2015
 PRESENTATIONS

P1.  Adopted Headquarters Battalion of the 1st Marine Division Quarterly Recognition

  Mayor Schlicht presented certificates of commendation to "Marine of the Quarter" Lance
  Corporal Elijah Duke and "Noncommissioned Officer of the Quarter" Sergeant Jaime
  Andrade.

P2.  Recognize Bruce Hunt as a Home Town Hero

  Mayor Schlicht presented a proclamation to Bruce Hunt.

P3.  Recognize Library Employee Alex Santo

  Mayor Schlicht presented a certificate of appreciation to Alex Santo.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Trish Kelley, M.V.: announced that there are two heroes in Mission Viejo who came to the aid of
a heart attack victim last week at the Sierra Recreation Center. Nora Latona, a registered nurse,
and staff member Jose Campos rushed to the man's aid and helped save his life.

Donna Varner, M.V.: on behalf of the Saddleback College Foundation, she invited the City
Council Members to the Foundation's gala on Saturday, March 14 at the Laguna Cliffs
Marriott. The event will benefit the students of Saddleback College and last year's contributions
amounted to $750,000. She encouraged the City to buy a table or for the Council Members to
attend individually.

Carole Weidler, M.V.: stated that she was astonished to learn that Mayor Schlicht issued
proclamations to her family members. She stated that without any Council discussion, this action
was in defiance of transparency in government and borders on the unethical.

Chuck McCullough: shared a listing of Chamber of Commerce events for the month of March,
including the monthly mixer, ribbon cutting ceremonies, and weekly networking meetings.

Wendy Allaire, M.V.: discussed fiscal accountability and she expressed concern with the cost of
median island landscaping that was estimated in the range of $550,000 but was approved by the
City Council in the amount of approximately $750,000.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Items 3 and 4 were removed from the Consent Calendar for separate discussion.

Motion made by Mayor Schlicht, seconded by Council Member Bucknum, to approve the Consent
Calendar as outlined below.

City Council Minutes  2  March 2, 2015
 On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, Schlicht, and Ury
NOES:  None
ABSENT: None

1.  Waive Reading of Ordinances and Resolutions

  Approved the reading by title of all ordinances and resolutions and declared that said titles
  which appear on the public agenda shall be determined to have been read by title and further
  reading waived.

2.  City Council Minutes

  Approved the Minutes for the Regular Meeting of February 16, 2015, as presented.

5.  Addition and Revisions to City of Mission Viejo Personnel Policies

  Adopted Resolution 15-10 Providing for the Establishment of and Revisions to Select
  Personnel Policies.

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

3.  Check Register Dated February 6, 2015 in the Amount of $794,688.48

  Mayor Schlicht referenced a payment to C&D Electric for holiday lights and stated
  that staff seems to be splitting invoices for the same item. She recommended that the City
  look at the bills before the next holiday season and consider going out to bid. Mayor
  Schlicht stated that she would love to find a way to decorate more of the street corners and
  by going out to bid, the cost might come down.

  Motion made by Mayor Schlicht, seconded by Council Member Sachs, to ratify the
  accompanying check register.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: None

4.  Check Register Dated February 13, 2015 in the Amount of $1,925,280.15

  Mayor Schlicht asked for a report on the number of animals that are coming in from the
  shard-services cities and how many animals are euthanized at the Mission Viejo
  animal shelter.

City Council Minutes  3  March 2, 2015
   Motion made by Mayor Schlicht, seconded by Council Member Sachs, to ratify the
  accompanying check register.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: None

OLD BUSINESS

6.  Contract with EventWerks to provide Food & Wine Festival at Arts Alive 2015

  Director of Library and Cultural Services Genesis Hansen presented the staff report and
  answered the Council Members' questions.

  Council Member Sachs asked that language be added to the contract to (1) address
  EventWerks' use of the term art festival, (2) clarify who holds liability if a member of the
  public becomes impaired due to drinking, and (3) attach a map to the contract which defines
  a restricted area for the consumption of alcoholic beverages.

  Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Council Member Sachs, to approve
  contract with EventWerks, as amended, and the one-time exemption to the "No Alcoholic
  Beverage Consumption "regulation at City Facilities to provide a Food & Wine Festival
  component in conjunction with this year's Arts Alive Festival on May 2 and 3, 2015
  (Amendments: add language to the contract to address EventWerks' use of the term art
  festival and who holds liability if a member of the public becomes impaired due to
  drinking.)

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: None

  Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Raths, to direct that
  the boundaries of the event serve as the area where alcohol consumption is allowed.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, and Ury
  NOES:  Sachs and Schlicht
  ABSENT: None

City Council Minutes  4  March 2, 2015
 7.  Repeal SFPA (Special Fire Protection Area)

  City Manager Wilberg presented the staff report and provided a history of the Special Fire
  Protection Area (SFPA) matter.

  Chief Lori Smith, Fire Marshall, Orange County Fire Authority: stated that she considered
  the City's existing ordinances and found that everything the City had in place prior to
  December 31, 1992, was sound and adequate to exempt the City of Mission Viejo from
  adopting the State fire maps.

  Trish Kelley, M.V.: discussed her work with former Mayor Reardon to protect the residents
  from the State mandate to adopt the severe fire maps. She noted that they crafted a solution
  that did no harm to the residents and basically threw out the severe fire hazard maps that
  were affecting over 3,000 homes. She stated that the Council should make certain that the
  action to remove the SFPA does not impact residents and put them back on to the State fire
  hazard maps.

  Rhonda Reardon, M.V.: asked the Council to consider delaying this action until the Council
  knows exactly what is going to happen with the State fire maps.

  Dennis O'Connor, representing the Orange County Association of Realtors, M.V.: stated
  that OCAR's number one priority is to advocate for homeowners. He said that this is a
  very confusing topic and he asked why the Council is bothering to revisit this when the
  problem was solved two years ago.

  Rita Tayenaka, President of the Orange County Association of Realtors, M.V.: asked why
  the City is doing this now. Two years ago, the Council acted to keep local control and she
  asked what has changed.

  Debbie Peel, M.V.: asked the Council to not support the repeal of the ordinance that created
  the SFPA. She stated that the action would be premature and she doesn't think it is wise to
  take the State by faith.

  Larry Gilbert, M.V.: asked the City Council for a yes vote on the repeal of the SFPA and
  he stated that the people of Mission Viejo want it changed.

  Cynthia Cantrelle, San Juan Capistrano, Vice President of the Saddleback Republican
  Assembly: read from a Saddleback Republican Assembly resolution which calls on the
  City Council to repeal the SFPA as an unnecessary layer of government.

  Matt Corrigan, M.V.: stated that he has heard a lot of retelling of history. He thanked
  Council Member Sachs for bringing this up for repeal and he stated that mistakes can be
  remedied.

City Council Minutes  5  March 2, 2015
   The following presented written comments in favor of repealing the Special Fire Protection
  Area: Gerald Volomino, M.V.; Stan and Leona Harris, M.V.; Gabriele Weidemahn, M.V.;
  Gregg and Janel Hooper, M.V.; Cary and Jinah Mocanu, M.V.; and Connie Lee, M.V. 29
  residents (many names illegible) also signed form letters in support of repealing the SFPA
  and prior to the Council Meeting, the City received 59 emails in support of the repeal and
  one email in opposition to the repeal of the SFPA.

  Chief Tonya Hoover, California State Fire Marshall: answered the City Council Members
  questions.

  Motion made by Council Member Sachs, seconded by Mayor Schlicht, to (1) adopt
  Ordinance 15-304 Repealing Ordinance 12-294 In Part, as it Previously Repealed
  Ordinance 95-151 (Designation Very High Fire Hazard Severity Zones) and Amended its
  Ordinance 10-287 to Delete the Defined Terms "Fire Hazard Severity Zones", "Local
  Agency Very High Fire Hazard Severity Zone" and "Wildland-Urban Interface Fire Area"
  and in all Instances of Use Substituting the Term "Special Fire Protection Area" or "SFPA",
  for all Purposes, as Further Defined Herein, as Amended (change the word and (2) adopt
  Resolution 15-11 Excluding all Areas Identified as a Very High Fire Hazard Severity Zone
  in the City of Mission Viejo and Adopting Findings Supported By Substantial Evidence in
  the Record Confirming Said Determination and Superseding and Termination of
  Resolution 12-47, as Amended (change the word consent to non-rebuttal.)

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: None

RECESS

At the hour of 8:01 p.m., Mayor Schlicht declared a recess. The City council reconvened at 8:14
p.m. with all five City Council Members present.

NEW BUSINESS

8.  Marguerite Aquatics Complex - Facility Review Needs Assessment Study

  Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services Keith Rattay presented the staff report.

  The following spoke in support of improvements to the Nadadores facility: Curt Wilson,
  San Clemente; Kris Yellin, Nadadores Foundation Board Member, M.V.; The Smith
  Family, M.V.; Suzi Fitzpatrick, M.V.; Lisa Muller, Irvine; Harold Epps, M.V.; Mark Gohr,
  Nadadores Foundation Board Member, M.V.; Thomas Ashbrook, President of the
  Nadadores Foundation Board of Directors, M.V.; and Dan O'Connor, M.V.

City Council Minutes  6  March 2, 2015
   The following stated that the Nadadores need to conduct fundraising to help pay for the
  improvements and that there be increased public access to the facility: Larry Gilbert, M.V.
  and Stephen Wontrobski, M.V. Prior to the meeting, Gail Reavis, M.V. sent an email with
  the same viewpoint on shared costs and public access.

  The following presented written comments in support of renovating the Nadadores facility:
  Debbie Peel, M.V.

  Council Member Sachs suggested that City staff and the Nadadores look at an opportunity
  for the City to offer a lease buy-back of 49% for certain "nice to have" improvements and
  he requested that staff provide a time table for individual projects at the facility.

  Thomas Ashbrook, President of the Nadadores Foundation Board of Directors: answered
  the City Council Members questions.

  Council Member Raths noted that he is working on finding a sponsor or sponsors to help
  cover some of the costs of the improvements.

  Motion made by Mayor Schlicht, seconded by Council Member Bucknum, to refer the
  needs assessment study to the Community Services Commission for their oversight, for
  public discussion and input, and for a recommendation back to the City Council. Directed
  that the Commission evaluate the suggestion to look at lease-back provisions.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: None

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, COMMITTEE REPORTS AND ACTIONS

9.  Orange County Fire Authority (OCFA) Report

  Council Member Sachs presented the report.

10.  Orange County Transportation Authority (OCTA)

  Council Member Ury presented the report.

STAFF REPORTS

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

11.  Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended

City Council Minutes  7  March 2, 2015
   The City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars as presented
  in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the public record.

Council Member Bucknum

Council Member Bucknum outlined her attendance at recent events including the Orange County
Business Council annual dinner where the board of directors were installed and the South and
North Mission Viejo Little League grand opening ceremonies. She stated that she was honored to
speak at the Local Agency Formation Commission (LAFCO) on shared services and she thanked
staff for preparing some information for that presentation. Council Member Bucknum also
discussed her attendance at the Economic Coalition’s economic report presentation at Saddleback
College and she thanked the people who helped a heart attack victim at the Sierra Recreation
Center last week. She noted that it was great to honor the Marines earlier this evening and although
it is sad to see Bruce Hunt stepping down as President of the Marine Adoption Committee, she
said that Gayle Woods will do a fantastic job. Council Member Bucknum thanked Bruce Hunt for
the great work he has done to help our veterans and she welcomed John Abel, the City’s new
OCFA division chief. She further thanked the OCFA and CalFire representatives who came to the
meeting tonight and helped to clarify the issues. Council Member Bucknum mentioned the
prescription drug use rally on Sunday that began at the civic center courtyard and then progressed
to the street corners. It was an attempt to raise awareness about the prescription drug problem with
our teens and she gave kudos to Jodi Barber for keeping that going. Council Member Bucknum
concluded her comments by announcing that the Community of Character word for the month of
March is service and she thanked all those who provide behind-the-scenes service to the
community.

Council Member Sachs

No report given.

Council Member Ury

No report given.

12.  Discuss Key Provisions of the Nadadores Contract

  This matter was discussed with agenda item 8.

Mayor Schlicht

Mayor Schlicht shared a quote from St. Francis, "Start by doing what's necessary then do what's
possible and suddenly you're doing the impossible."

City Council Minutes  8  March 2, 2015
 Mayor Pro Tem Raths

Mayor Pro Tem Raths stated that he is so impressed with all the new businesses that are coming
to the City. He discussed his attendance at the ribbon cutting ceremony for Club Pilates and an
awards ceremony at the Oxford Preparatory Academy. He also had the honor of attending an
Eagle Scout ceremony which was very special to him as he and his four brothers are Eagle
Scouts. Mayor Pro Tem Raths announced that his father, John A. Raths, recently passed away at
the age of 96. Born in 1918, John was a World War II combat A-20 pilot, was the father of eight
children and was married to Mayor Pro Tem Raths’ mother for 56 years before she passed away 7
years ago. Mayor Pro Tem Raths announced that he would adjourn the meeting in memory of his
father.

ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 9:55 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session,
Mayor Pro Tem Raths adjourned the meeting in memory of John A. Raths, to Monday, March 16,
2015, at 5:00 p.m.

______________________________________________
Karen Hamman, City Clerk

Approved at the meeting of March 16, 2015

City Council Minutes  9  March 2, 2015
